pr.title: Sign a reviewed head off with labels and a status, not draft state
pr.head: 575d040f94ab754955b8329956a11f35efa2eea0

summary: Projector reviews pull requests for their author and publishes a verdict on each head. On the author's own pull request GitHub refuses both an approval and a change request, so until now Projector carried the verdict in draft state: project review publish converted the pull request to a draft when a review found problems and marked it ready when a review was clean. That left the author no way to say "I'm still working", so every head got a full review, including heads replaced minutes later.

This pull request is the first of three layers that give draft back its GitHub meaning. It moves the sign-off to two other places. A head is signed off when the newest counted Projector verdict on it, from any model, is clean and no Projector finding thread is open. publish then labels the pull request clean, and posts a projector/review commit status on the reviewed commit wherever a ruleset on the default branch requires that status. setup adds a reviewing label while a review runs. The author's hold comment goes, and two commands, project review hold and project review ready, move the author's own draft state.

The layers above add the daemon's wait for a pull request to be ready (#426) and project init's setup of the required check and the label workflow (#427). Until they land, this layer still reviews every head, draft or not.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Sign-off: the newest counted verdict on the head is clean and no finding thread is open. sign_off in review.py decides it.
  • clean label: the list-visible view of the sign-off.
  • reviewing label: a review's start comment is live.
  • projector/review: the commit status a ruleset can require before a merge.
  • Hold: converting your own signed-off pull request to a draft while you build a change on it.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first Projector review of 575d040 requested changes with one finding: fix-pr reads the sign-off from the clean label, which review.labels = false or a refused label edit leaves off. It also listed two suggestions.

groups.title: Sign-off in the review commands
groups.kicker: How setup, publish, status, and finish decide and show the sign-off
intro: publish no longer runs gh pr ready. After it submits, it re-reads the verdicts and the open finding threads, and sign_off decides whether the head is signed off. It then dismisses standing change requests on another author's signed-off pull request, posts the status when requires_check finds a ruleset that requires it, and changes both labels in one gh pr edit. A refused status fails the run, and a rerun finishes it without a second review. A refused label edit only warns.

setup adds reviewing and takes off a clean that no clean verdict on the new head supports, which covers a repository with no label workflow. hold and ready replace the hold comment's code, and review.labels = false turns the labels off.

groups.title: The daemon's re-review request
groups.kicker: RESPONDED now fires only on a change request
intro: Before this change the daemon also asked for a re-review of the author's own draft, because draft meant "not signed off", and it read the hold comment. Draft no longer means that, so RESPONDED fires only when the head's newest verdict requests changes and the author answered. The daemon's query also reads each pull request's labels for the panel.

files.note: The simplified RESPONDED condition, is_held removed, and labels in the query.

groups.title: The panel's review state
groups.kicker: Each row says reviewing, draft, clean, or ready
intro: Projector's panel in Claude Code lists the session's pull requests. A row used to print draft or ready. It now prints the first of reviewing, draft, clean, and ready that applies, and only clean is green, so a held draft that keeps its clean label reads as a draft.

groups.title: Skills and generated instructions
groups.kicker: What agents do with draft state now
intro: Agents still open every pull request as a draft, and now mark it ready with project review ready once their work is done, or once the person answers a test request. fix-pr holds a signed-off pull request by converting it to a draft while it builds a suggestion, and marks it ready after the push. The generated instructions block moves to version 25.
